failure_summary.description: Answers used a shortened or familiar personal name, omitted an integral identifying element, or appended a generic category word to a requested nickname.
Answers selected a related property or contextual fact instead of the referent or term required by the clue's exact wording.

patch.reasoning: Clarify the subtle distinction between a complete identifying form and a requested nickname component. The other failures concern relation and clue interpretation, which the existing skill already addresses, so adding another general rule would be redundant.

edits.target: Use a full canonical personal name when the clue does not supply a name component; when it supplies part of a name and asks for completion, give only the missing component.
edits.content: For a named person, use the conventional identifying form supported by the clue, including a surname or regnal numeral when needed; do not substitute a familiar nickname for a formal name directly supported by context. If the clue asks for a nickname, epithet, or alias and already supplies the entity type, return the requested distinguishing label without reattaching a generic type word. Supply only a missing name component when the prompt explicitly asks to complete a supplied name; otherwise give the answer form that fills the requested slot.
